subject: french
title: Days of the Week
welcome_lead: Lundi to dimanche — the French week.
meta_desc: KS3 French: days of the week.
final_note: French days have planetary names like English.

walkthroughs.body_html: The French week starts with lundi. Then: mardi, mercredi, jeudi, vendredi, samedi, dimanche. Notice that French days do not have capital letters.
'Today is.' = Aujourd'hui c'est.. So 'Aujourd'hui c'est mardi' = today is Tuesday. Demain = tomorrow, hier = yesterday.
To say 'on Mondays' (every Monday) use le lundi. 'Le samedi je joue au football' = 'On Saturdays I play football'.

mcqs.q: When do you use the imperfect rather than the passé composé?
options: When you don't know what tense to use.
Either is fine in modern French.
For ongoing, habitual, or descriptive past actions.

mcqs.q: When meeting a teacher or stranger for the first time, do you use 'tu' or 'vous'?
options: Either is fine in modern French.
When you don't know what tense to use.
Tu, because it's singular and you're talking to one person.
